content.description: Cold, fear, music: chills have several causes. They all run through the nervous system, but not for the same reasons.

hero.hook: A chill from the cold and a chill from music do not tell the same story.

blocks.text: You shiver when you step out into the rain. You also get chills when you hear a song that moves you. Same word, different mechanisms.
In both cases the body reacts fast. But one is mainly there to warm you up, while the other has more to do with pleasure and emotion.
The body wants to stay around **37°C**. When the skin detects cold, it alerts an area of the brain, the **hypothalamus**, which acts as a thermostat.

blocks.caption: Goosebumps: an old reflex for raising the hairs

blocks.text: The muscles contract very fast, over and over, and that is shivering. Those contractions produce heat. “Goosebumps” come from an old reflex, raising the hairs to insulate better. In humans, with so little fur, they are mostly a leftover.

sections.title: The chill of cold: a tiny furnace

blocks.text: Faced with a threat, the [[sympathetic nervous system]] (the “alert” branch of the nervous system) switches on. It releases **adrenaline**. The muscles tense, the heart speeds up, and the skin can shiver.

blocks.caption: Adrenaline gets the body ready to react fast

blocks.text: That same system explains why you can get goosebumps watching a horror movie, even though you are warm and safe on your couch.
Some chills, sometimes called “frisson,” come with a strong emotion: music, a speech, a film. They light up the brain's **reward** circuit, with **dopamine**, a substance linked to pleasure.
This one is no help for immediate survival. It is more the body answering an intense emotion, like a wave passing through.

Chills with a high fever can signal an infection. Constant chills with no clear cause deserve a medical opinion. But most of the time, a chill from cold, stress, or music is simply the body doing its job.
Chills from cold produce heat. Chills from fear get you ready to react. Chills from music touch on emotional pleasure. Same sensation, different causes.

content.title: Why do we get chills?

Chills.explanation: A series of rapid and involuntary muscle contractions intended to produce heat or reflecting strong nervous excitement.

Dopamine.explanation: Chemical neurotransmitter in the brain playing a central role in the reward circuit, pleasure, and motivation.

Hypothalamus.explanation: Structure located at the base of the brain that regulates vital functions such as hunger, thirst, or body temperature (the biological thermostat).

The autonomic nervous system.explanation: Part of the nervous system responsible for the body's automatic functions (digestion, heart rate, temperature) without voluntary control.

The sympathetic nervous system.explanation: Branch of the autonomic nervous system that prepares the body for action ("fight or flight"). Faced with a threat, it triggers adrenaline, accelerates the heart, dilates the pupils, and contracts the arrector pili muscles - the chills of fear.

quiz.explanation: When the skin detects cold, it alerts the hypothalamus, an area of the brain that acts as a body thermostat.
quiz.question: Which area of the brain acts as a thermostat when the skin detects cold?

quiz.explanation: Shivering comes from rapid, repeated muscle contractions, which produce heat to warm the body.
options: Muscles contract very quickly and repeatedly
The skin directly absorbs heat from the air
The heart stops for a few seconds
quiz.question: Why do cold shivers produce heat?

quiz.explanation: Goosebumps are an old reflex that raises the hairs to better insulate the body, even if it no longer serves much purpose in humans with little hair.
quiz.question: True or false: goosebumps come from an old reflex which served to raise the hairs to better insulate from the cold.

quiz.explanation: When faced with a threat, the sympathetic nervous system releases adrenaline, which tenses the muscles and accelerates the heart.
quiz.question: What substance does the sympathetic nervous system release when faced with a threat?

quiz.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system reacts to the fear felt while watching the film, even without real danger, which triggers goosebumps.
options: The alert nervous system reacts to fear, as if there were a real threat
The room temperature always drops during a scary movie
This is only a reaction to the loud noise in the film
The body chemically confuses film and reality
quiz.question: Why can you get goosebumps while watching a horror film, cozy on your couch?

quiz.explanation: Musical thrills activate the brain's reward circuit, with dopamine, a substance linked to pleasure.
quiz.question: What pleasure-related substance is associated with the thrills felt while listening to upsetting music?

quiz.explanation: These shivers share the word but not the mechanism: cold produces heat, fear prepares us to react, music touches emotional pleasure.
quiz.question: True or false: the shivers of cold, fear and music all go through the same mechanism, with the same goal.

quiz.explanation: Chills accompanied by high fever, or constant chills without a clear cause, may signal a problem and merit medical attention.
options: Chills with a high fever, or constant chills for no clear reason
Every time we shiver while listening to music
Every time we feel cold in winter
As soon as we watch a moving film
quiz.question: When should chills cause concern and merit medical advice?
